rationale: Baseline and resumed lineage run the same image, device class and thread count with torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True), a self-managed sampler whose epoch permutation derives only from (seed, epoch), and a checkpoint that restores model, SGD momentum buffers and the Python/NumPy/torch CPU RNG exactly; a same-host resume is therefore expected to be bitwise equal, and the bitwise result is recorded only as information.

The tolerances bound what the contract does not promise: float32 CPU kernels may pick a different vectorised reduction order on another host of the same architecture (ISA dispatch), and SGD amplifies last-bit differences over the steps of a run.

Losses are float64 means of per-item cross-entropy whose scale is ln(10) ~ 2.3 before training; 0.001 absolute is below 0.05% of that scale and far below any change a skipped or duplicated batch would cause.
eval_accuracy is a count over the fixed 1000-item eval split, so 0.005 admits at most five predictions flipping at a decision boundary and nothing larger.

Norms are float64 sums of float32 tensors; 1e-4 relative is about three orders of magnitude above float32 epsilon and still catches any lost optimizer state, since a momentum reset or a missing update changes the norms by far more.
Sample coverage, step/epoch/cursor, checksums and provenance have no tolerance: they are integers or digests and must match exactly.

These values are argued from the fixture design before any acceptance measurement; development measurements are never used to tune them, and a measurement outside them is a finding, not a reason to widen them.
